gen-dafont-electroharmonix-instrument-sa: Gappy, loud, split into single letters. Instrument Sans follows in a plain sans with unvarying strokes and a minimal step from capitals to lowercase, so a long passage glides along without a snag.
gen-dafont-electroharmonix-switzer: Commanding gaps cut each Electroharmonix word into separate letters, while Switzer keeps its tall waist line and wire-like tubular forms. One shouts in pieces; the other speaks in plain sans lines.
gen-dafont-eraser-fs-familjen-grotesk: Understated yet firm, Eraser draws bold letters with no thick-thin shifts at all. Familjen Grotesk brings the opposite energy: a tall lowercase and bowls left open on one side, which is the pair's liveliest quality.
gen-dafont-eraser-fs-hoover: Heavy, flat, uniform letters up top. Hoover, a classic serif with compressed ascenders and a generous entry into the e, wants its body size nudged a touch larger than feels natural, since Eraser's weight is doing the shouting.
gen-dafont-eraser-fs-ranade: Eraser's bold letters carry no thick or thin strokes anywhere, as if drawn with a round-tipped pen. Ranade, a plain sans with slightly stretching weight and far-apart stroke ends, spreads out gently down the page.
gen-dafont-espresso-dolce-fs-erode: Erode sets a tall middle band with shallow ascenders, a broad g and a, and a gentle ebb of stroke weight. And Espresso Dolce adds its calligraphic hand and wide-eyed e, glowing like neon tubing above that serif.
gen-dafont-espresso-dolce-fs-spline-sans: Espresso Dolce writes in a calligraphic hand with neon-tube thickness, then hands off to Spline Sans, a plain sans with identical weight in vertical and horizontal strokes. Best kept to modest paragraphs.
gen-dafont-ethnocentric-fs-familjen-grot: Aggressive, fast and spaced wide, Ethnocentric pushes its letters apart over big bowls and short ascenders. But Familjen Grotesk, a sans with tall lowercase and half-open bowls, lets a long passage move along with ease.
gen-dafont-ethnocentric-fs-karma: Fast and aggressive, Ethnocentric stretches wide. Karma, a text serif with terminals well clear of the stem and a gentle swell in its rounds, is where the pair's trustworthy side lives, grounding all that speed.
gen-dafont-ethnocentric-fs-ranade: Ranade runs as a plain sans with slightly tapered, glass-rod strokes and widely spaced ends. Ethnocentric is the one to make a bold, fast statement, while Ranade handles quiet, organic running text.
